blocks.title: First electron affinity
blocks.text: The first electron affinity, delta Hea, is the enthalpy change when one mole of electrons is added to one mole of gaseous atoms to form one mole of gaseous uni-negative ions under standard conditions.

For chlorine, Cl(g) + e- gives Cl-(g), delta H = -348.8 kJ per mol; energy is released, so the first electron affinity carries a negative sign. A detailed discussion of electron affinity is given in chapter 1.

blocks.prompt: The first electron affinity of sulfur is -200 kJ per mol and the second is +640 kJ per mol. Find delta H for S(g) + 2e- giving S2-(g), and explain the sign of the second affinity.
blocks.explanation: Adding the two steps: -200 + 640 = +440 kJ per mol. The second electron must be pushed onto an ion that is already negative, against its repulsion, so energy is absorbed and the second affinity is positive.

items: First electron affinity: one mole of gaseous atoms gaining one mole of electrons to give gaseous uni-negative ions; negative because energy is released (Cl -348.8 kJ per mol); a second affinity is positive.
